name: Wendover Woods 50
place: Trig Point Field, Aston Hill, Halton
transport: Start and finish at Trig Point Field, HP22 5NQ; check organiser parking instructions
facilities: Two aid locations revisited across five loops; drop bag accessible every 10 miles
reason: Five 10-mile forest loops simplify finish logistics but pack 10,000ft of climbing into 50 miles. The 15-hour clock and intermediate cut-offs make sustained climbing pace decisive.
course: Five 10-mile loops on Wendover Woods trails and tracks; some road crossings are unstaffed.
rules: A prior marathon-distance race finish is required; no pacers or crew. Check mandatory kit and lighting rules for later loops.

name: ABP Newport Half
place: Newport city centre and Gwent Levels
cutoff: 4 hours for Run 4 Wales half marathons; confirm event-specific timing
transport: City-centre riverfront start and finish; confirm road closures and arrival plan
reason: A Newport riverfront start and finish with a route into the Gwent Levels. It shares festival day with the marathon and 10K, so check the half-marathon start and baggage instructions specifically.
start: Newport riverfront; half-marathon wave time to confirm.
course: City centre to the Gwent Levels and back; final route map to check.
rules: Check the half-marathon participant pack, especially start time and any course changes.

name: Kensington 10K
transport: Start and finish beside Holland Park, off Kensington High Street; check road closures and station access
reason: A single-lap, closed-road 10K through Kensington and Notting Hill. Its Holland Park start and finish simplify return travel; confirm the final arrival area and road closures before booking.
start: Beside Holland Park; start time to confirm.
course: Single lap through Kensington and Notting Hill, including Portobello Road.
rules: Check the final event page for age limit, race cut-off and baggage arrangements.

name: Gloucester Half Marathon and 10K
elevation: 75m on half-marathon route; 10km ascent not confirmed
transport: Gloucester station is near the start; no dedicated event parking
facilities: Secure bag drop, toilets, route water and event village
reason: A city-and-canal race with some gravel underfoot. The three-hour road-closure limit and lack of dedicated parking matter more than the relatively low half-marathon ascent.
course: Gloucester Park, city centre and cathedral, Quedgeley and canal path; closed roads and gravel sections.
rules: Minimum ages 17 for half marathon and 15 for 10km. Check final route and closure notices.

name: Victoria Park Spring Running Festival
transport: Use Hackney Wick, Mile End, Bow Road or Homerton stations; nearby parking is limited
facilities: Secure bag drop, toilets, route water and finish refreshments
reason: Wide, flat park paths suit a measured effort, but the three distances have separate starts and the 5K and half-marathon lines are a walk from the event village.
course: Multiple park-path laps; confirm exact lap count for chosen distance.
rules: Dogs cannot run; buggy runners and wheelchair athletes are welcomed. Check final pack for route details.

name: Battersea Park Spring Running Festival
transport: Millennium Track start; confirm park entrance and travel before race day
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and finish support
reason: A flat park route with a later 10:30 half-marathon start. The 5K and 10K start close together, so use your own race-pack time rather than the headline event time.
course: Flat Battersea Park circuit; lap counts to confirm by distance.
rules: Contact the organiser before entering if likely to exceed the published distance-specific limit.
